---
title: "Week 12: Generics & traits"
---

## Introduction

This week covers two tools for writing code once and using it with many types. Generics let a function, struct, or enum use a placeholder type `T` that the compiler fills in. Traits name what a type can do, and trait bounds connect the two: "any `T` that can be compared." We'll start from duplicated code, read compiler errors that explain why a bound is needed, and finish by building a generic `Stack<T>` that prints itself with `Display`.

- [Section 10.2: Traits](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch10-02-traits.html) - Session 2 follows this section's examples. Section 10.3 on lifetimes was the optional extension in Week 10
